source_text.body:
Spawn a new Claude Code session from a to-do list
An agent (Fable) controlled the mouse in Claude Code Desktop, opened a new session mid-task and pasted a to-do item into it.
·
Jul 20, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The poster had Fable make a to-do list from a long Claude Code session that had gone off track, then manually pasted that list into a fresh session. Midway through working, Fable used the computer-control permission they had granted it to move the mouse in Claude Code Desktop, click New Session, and paste in one task from its own to-do list; in comments, the poster says they had allowed Fable to use the PC and thinks a leader-worker setup may have enabled it.
How it went
It successfully spun up another Claude Code session on its own from the UI, which surprised the user because they had only seen it use the PC for testing before. The thread gives no performance numbers or clear result beyond that behavior.
Worth knowing
The main catch is permissions: the poster says they had set Fable to always allow computer use, and later noticed their leader agent may have had too much power.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
In Claude Code Desktop, while my current task is running, open a new session and paste in this to-do item: [to-do text]. Don't interrupt or change the original session. Stop once the new session has the text pasted, and do not submit it until I confirm.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/Anthropic/comments/1ux9q6b/fable_controlled_my_claude_code_desktop_to_create
